error_modes.label: Flaps LDG / T-O / AOA landing - touchdown point control
error_modes.source: specific:TOUCH DOWN POINT (feet from the beginning of the RWY) [a/ FLAPS LDG - FLAPS T/O - AOA] (ref contact-24)

texts.0: SP, due to a late round out flown with residual power after the formation approach, did not bring the A/C to the touchdown point as described in the Flight Manuals. The A/C floated in ground effect and contacted the RWY beyond 1500 ft from the beginning of the RWY, outside the landing criteria. The IP took the controls to close the throttle and place the A/C on the RWY. The aim point was neither selected nor protected during the level off.
texts.1: SP, due to a delayed power reduction while the aim point was reacquired after the lateral repositioning from the formation, carried excess energy into the level off. Touchdown was achieved at the 1500 ft limit from the beginning of the RWY, and only after the IP called for the power to be closed and the landing attitude to be held. SP did not recognize the developing float from the A/C response before the verbal prompt.
texts.2: SP, due to a round out started slightly high, allowed a short float before contact with the RWY. Touchdown occurred between 1000 and 1500 ft from the beginning of the RWY. SP recognized the float, held the landing attitude and completed the touchdown in time, with no intervention from the IP.
texts.3: SP executed the round out timely, levelled off the A/C, assumed the landing attitude and brought the A/C in touch with the RWY as described in the Flight Manuals. Touchdown was achieved within 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY, on the selected aim point. The gradual power reduction and the control of the rate of descent were consistent from the end of the formation approach to contact.
texts.4: SP flew the round out and the flare with precise power and attitude control, placing the A/C on the selected aim point with negligible dispersion between repeated landings. Touchdown was achieved comfortably within 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY, with no float and no late correction. Aim point discipline was maintained through the transition from the formation approach to the individual landing.
texts.marginal: SP touched down within the required 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY, but consistently at the far end of that band. The tendency is a round out started slightly high after the transition from the formation, which produces a brief float and moves the touchdown point long. SP is expected to begin the gradual power reduction earlier and to hold the landing attitude with less float, so that the touchdown point is centred on the aim point rather than at the limit.

texts_at.0: SP flew the round out and the level off with the IP demonstrating the timing of the power reduction and calling the landing attitude through the flare. The touchdown point after the formation approach has not been set by SP alone yet, and the aim point selection is still new at this stage. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to begin selecting and protecting the aim point without the IP's lead-in on the next approach.
texts_at.1: SP brought the A/C to the touchdown point at the 1500 ft limit from the beginning of the RWY, after a delayed power reduction during the reacquisition of the aim point following the lateral repositioning from the formation carried extra energy into the level off and left the developing float unrecognized until the IP called for the power to be closed and the landing attitude held. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to recognize the developing float from the A/C response before the verbal prompt on the next approach.
texts_at.2: SP brought the A/C to the touchdown point between 1000 and 1500 ft from the beginning of the RWY, after a round out that started slightly high produced a short float SP recognized and held through to a landing attitude without any prompting from the IP. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to start the round out a fraction lower so that the float, and the distance it adds to the touchdown point, is reduced.
texts_at.3: SP brought the A/C in touch with the RWY within 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY on the selected aim point, though consistently toward the far end of that band after a round out that starts a shade high following the transition from the formation approach. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to begin the round out a fraction lower so the touchdown point sits closer to the aim point than to the edge of the band.

texts_above.1: SP brought the A/C to the touchdown point at the 1500 ft limit from the beginning of the RWY, holding the landing attitude through the float that followed the level off. The power reduction and the landing attitude call followed a verbal prompt from the IP. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP brought the A/C to the touchdown point between 1000 and 1500 ft from the beginning of the RWY, recognizing a round out that started slightly high and holding the landing attitude through the resulting float without any prompting from the IP. Setting the round out a touch lower would remove the float before it starts. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to good round-out recognition after the transition from the formation approach.
texts_above.3: SP flew the round out and the level off on schedule and brought the A/C in touch with the RWY within 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY, on the selected aim point, with the power reduction and the rate of descent controlled smoothly from the end of the formation approach through contact. The only refinement available is to hold the same picture on the shorter fields used later in the syllabus. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to very good energy control through the level off.
texts_above.4: SP placed the A/C on the selected aim point with negligible float on every landing, holding the touchdown point comfortably inside 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY with no late correction needed at any point in the flare. Aim point discipline carried across the transition from the formation approach without a single adjustment between repetitions. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to excellent aim-point discipline through the round out and flare.

error_modes.label: Flaps LDG / T-O / AOA landing - lateral placement and centerline deviation at touchdown
error_modes.source: specific:DEVIATION FROM CENTER LINE (feet) [a/ FLAPS LDG - FLAPS T/O - AOA] (ref contact-24)|general(ref contact-24):a,f

texts.0: SP, due to an unremoved crab carried from the formation approach, did not direct the A/C to the RWY centerline reference. The A/C touched down more than 15 ft laterally displaced from that reference and with a drift, outside the landing criteria. The IP took the controls to align the A/C and stop the lateral movement during the roll-out. SP neither applied the crosswind controls nor executed a go-around.
texts.1: SP, due to insufficient rudder input during the level off, left the A/C offset from the RWY centerline reference. Touchdown was achieved at the 15 ft lateral limit, and the alignment was corrected only after the IP called for rudder and into-wind aileron. SP did not detect the lateral displacement from the outside references before the prompt.
texts.2: SP, due to a slightly late removal of the crab after the transition from the formation, touched down laterally displaced from the RWY centerline reference by between 5 and 15 ft. SP identified the offset during the level off, applied rudder and into-wind aileron and stopped the drift before contact, with no intervention from the IP.
texts.3: SP directed the A/C to the RWY centerline reference, removed the crab before contact and touched down within 5 ft of it, with the longitudinal axis aligned with the direction of the roll-out. Crosswind controls were applied progressively through the level off, and no drift was present at touchdown. The alignment was held throughout the deceleration.
texts.4: SP held the A/C on the RWY centerline reference from the end of the formation approach to contact, with negligible lateral deviation and no perceptible drift at touchdown. Crosswind controls were applied continuously and in the correct proportion, so that no lateral correction was required during the roll-out.
texts.marginal: SP touched down within the required 5 ft of the RWY centerline reference, but consistently displaced to the same side. The tendency is a residual crab that is removed late, so the alignment is achieved just before contact rather than during the level off. SP is expected to establish the wing-low, rudder-aligned technique earlier so that the lateral placement is centred rather than at the edge of the acceptable band.

texts_at.0: SP flew the level off and the crab removal with the IP calling the rudder and aileron inputs needed to hold the RWY centerline reference. Removing the crab in coordination with the round out after the formation approach is still a new sequence at this stage. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to begin the crab removal without the IP's calls on the next approach.
texts_at.1: SP touched down at the 15 ft lateral limit from the RWY centerline reference, after insufficient rudder input during the level off left the A/C offset and the alignment was corrected only once the IP called for rudder and into-wind aileron. texts_at.2: SP touched down between 5 and 15 ft laterally displaced from the RWY centerline reference, after a slightly late removal of the crab following the transition from the formation, identifying the offset and applying rudder and into-wind aileron to stop the drift before contact without any intervention from the IP. texts_at.3: SP touched down within 5 ft of the RWY centerline reference, though consistently displaced to the same side after a residual crab that is removed only just before contact rather than during the level off. texts_above.1: SP touched down at the 15 ft lateral limit from the RWY centerline reference, correcting the alignment through the level off. texts_above.2: SP touched down between 5 and 15 ft laterally displaced from the RWY centerline reference, identifying a crab removed slightly late after the transition from the formation and applying rudder and into-wind aileron to stop the drift before contact without any prompting from the IP. Starting the crab removal with the level off, rather than after it, would close the remaining margin. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to sound rudder and aileron coordination in the flare.
texts_above.3: SP directed the A/C to the RWY centerline reference, removed the crab before contact and touched down within 5 ft of it, with the longitudinal axis aligned to the direction of the roll-out and crosswind controls applied progressively through the level off. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to sure-handed crosswind control through the level off.
texts_above.4: SP held the A/C on the RWY centerline reference from the end of the formation approach to contact, with negligible lateral deviation and no perceptible drift at touchdown on any of the landings flown. Crosswind controls were applied continuously and in the correct proportion, so no lateral correction was required during the roll-out. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to exceptional centerline discipline through the level off.
